alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 23 at 3:44AM HST until September 26 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
An intensifying tropical cyclone is expected to bring heavy rain to
the eastern end of the state over the next few days. The exact track
of the dangerous tropical cyclone remains somewhat uncertain, but
significant heavy rain is likely over windward and southeast Big
Island.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Big Island, Maui, Lanai, Molokai, and Kahoolawe.

* WHEN...From noon HST today through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain on the north side of an intensifying tropical cyclone
will develop later today and tonight over Big Island and spread
to Maui. Windward and southeast Big Island and windward Maui are
the most likely to experience heavy rain, with considerable
flooding possible over portions of Big Island Friday into the
weekend. Other islands in Maui County are at risk as well.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Tropical Weather Outlook

Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Wed Sep 23 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located a couple of hundred miles offshore of southern
Mexico, on recently upgraded Hurricane Odalys, located well
west-southwest of the southern tip of Baja California, and on
recently re-formed Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located a few
hundred miles south-southeast of the Big Island of Hawaii.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

aiBriefing: Dziś (23 września) obowiązuje ostrzeżenie przed powodzią (Flood Watch) dla wielu rejonów Hawajów, w tym Big Island, Maui, Lanai i Molokai, ważne do soboty 26 września wieczorem — to skutek intensyfikującej się depresji tropikalnej Fifteen-E, która jest obecnie około 840 km od trasy. Wasza podróż zaczyna się dopiero za 8 dni, czyli 2 października, więc to konkretne ostrzeżenie i sam system Fifteen-E powinny się zakończyć na długo przed Waszym przylotem. Poziom zagrożenia jest ustawiony na 2 (Podwyższony) właśnie ze względu na tę aktywną, ale krótkoterminową sytuację pogodową, a nie z powodu czegoś, co dotyczy bezpośrednio Waszych dat na Oahu, Big Island czy Maui. Pozostałe huragany (Odalys, Polo) są bardzo daleko, w rejonie Meksyku, i nie mają znaczenia dla Waszej podróży. Warto jednak śledzić prognozy bliżej daty wylotu, na wypadek gdyby pojawił się nowy system.
